chapter: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
title: The Humphrey family and other trombonists
summary: He played with Willie and Earl Humphrey, comments on Earl's trombone, and on Zue Robertson and Frankie Duson.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you know any of the Humphrey family?
Willie Humphrey, Poisey Humphrey, and the other one, I forget his name now.
The trompon player was Earl.
By Earl, yeah.
And then the father was Willie.
It was Willie too, yeah.
And then there was Jim.
Yeah, Jim was the grandfather. The grandfather. You played with him as far? I played with Willie, I played with Oil, and I never played with Poisey. Willie and Oil played trombone with me.
Oh, he was with your band?
He was in the band, yeah.
The Nola band?
Yeah. Oh.
Yeah, he played. What about Willie? What band did you play then?
Well, I just played occasions with him. Excuse me, he was one of them.
You think Earl was a very good trombone player?

Well, I always thought he was, you know, he was attractive, he could attract your attention. Yeah. Yeah. Who do you think would have been a better trombone player to let you know? At that time, a fellow by the name of... I just might be his nickname. Niece, Zoo Robertson. Yeah. Yeah. He was real... Who you worked with him? I didn't know. I never worked with him, but I knew he was. Yeah. He was a real good trombone player. Uh-huh.
Did you know that?
And then they had another one, but he didn't read, uh, Frankie Doosen. I'm sure you might know him. Yeah.
I've seen his grave up across the river.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
McDonald's, though.
Did you know Eddie Morris? Eddie Morris?
I didn't know him. He's a favorite of the... Yeah. Punch. Yeah. I don't know. Maybe I might know him, but I'm not sure.
